definitions.explanation: The process of expressing thoughts, feelings, or abstract concepts in words. A popular concept in Japanese business and self-improvement discourse.

examples.japanese: ⟦{感覚|かんかく}→感覚：02593_kankaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{言語化|げんごか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To put a feeling into words.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{考|かんが}え→考え：00855_kangae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{言語化|げんごか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧だ。
examples.english: I'm not good at articulating my thoughts.

examples.japanese: なんとなく⟦{感|かん}じていた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧こと⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{言語化|げんごか}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦もらって→もらう：00520_morau⟧、⟦すっきり→すっきり：05180_sukkiri⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I felt relieved when someone put into words what I had been vaguely feeling.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{言語|げんご}→言語：02717_gengo⟧ (language) + ⟦{化|か}→〜化：28335_ka⟧ (transformation suffix, "-ization"). Has become a buzzword in Japanese business culture, self-help, and education, reflecting a growing emphasis on the ability to clearly express ideas.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {気持|きも}ち⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{言語化|げんごか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (verbalize one's feelings)
- {言語化|げんごか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{力|ちから}→力：01661_chikara⟧ (the ability to verbalize)
- {言語化|げんごか}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧ (difficult to put into words)
- {暗黙知|あんもくち}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{言語化|げんごか} (articulating tacit knowledge)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to put into words (more colloquial, everyday expression)
- ⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to express (broader, includes non-verbal expression)
- ⟦{明文化|めいぶんか}→明文化：13049_meibunka⟧ — codification, putting in written form (more formal, focuses on documentation)

USAGE:
The suffix ⟦{化|か}→〜化：28335_ka⟧ (-ization) is highly productive in Japanese. Similar formations include ⟦{可視化|かしか}→可視化：07644_kashika⟧ (visualization), ⟦{数値化|すうちか}→数値化：16461_suuchika⟧ (quantification), and ⟦{具体化|ぐたいか}→具体化：20775_gutaika⟧ (making concrete).
